variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
X = 10,
%% Variables must start with an uppercase letter.

%% Pattern matching binds variables
{A, B} = {1, 2}.
variables.notes: Variables are immutable and can only be bound once in a context. They must begin with an uppercase letter.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
Int = 42,
Float = 3.14,
Atom = ok,  %% Starts with lowercase
Tuple = {person, "Alice", 30},
List = [1, 2, 3],
Binary = <<"hello">>,
Pid = self().
data_types.notes: Erlang is dynamically typed. Atoms are constants with name as value. Pids represent concurrent actor processes.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
Add = 5 + 3,
Sub = 5 - 3,
Mul = 5 * 3,
DivFloat = 5 / 2,
DivInt = 5 div 2,
RemInt = 5 rem 2,

Logic = true andalso false orelse true,

Eq = 5 =:= 5, %% Exact equality
Neq = 5 =/= 3.
operators.notes: Variables assignment `=` is actually the pattern matching operator. Strict equality `=:=` compares both value and type.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: if expressions require at least one branch to evaluate to true. case expressions are preferred as they leverage pattern matching.

for_loop.title: For Loop (Comprehensions)
for_loop.code:
%% List comprehensions act as for loops
List = [1, 2, 3, 4, 5],
Squares = [X * X || X <- List],

%% Mapping
Mapped = lists:map(fun(X) -> X * 2 end, List).
for_loop.notes: Erlang has no traditional loops. List comprehensions and higher-order functions from the `lists` module handle iteration.

while_loop.title: While Loop (Recursion)
while_loop.code:
loop(0) -> 
    ok;
loop(N) ->
    io:format("~p~n", [N]),
    loop(N - 1).

%% State loops (Actor model)
actor_loop(State) ->
    receive
        {msg, Value} -> actor_loop(State + Value);
        stop -> ok
    end.
while_loop.notes: Loops are implemented via tail-recursion. In the BEAM VM, processes run recursive receive loops to maintain state.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
add(X, Y) -> 
    X + Y.

%% Multiple clauses with pattern matching
factorial(0) -> 1;
factorial(N) when N > 0 -> N * factorial(N - 1).

%% Anonymous function
Multiply = fun(X, Y) -> X * Y end.
functions.notes: Functions can have multiple clauses separated by `;`. The final clause ends with `.`. Guards (`when`) restrict clauses.

arrays.title: Lists and Tuples
arrays.code:
List1 = [1, 2, 3],
List2 = [0 | List1], %% Prepend (cons)
List3 = [1, 2] ++ [3, 4], %% Concat

%% Tuples for fixed collections
Point = {10, 20},
First = element(1, Point). %% 1-indexed
arrays.notes: Lists are singly-linked. Tuples are fixed-size and memory-efficient. No mutable arrays exist by default.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
Map = #{name => "Alice", age => 30},

%% Update/Insert (=>)
Map1 = Map#{city => "London"},

%% Update existing key (:=)
Map2 = Map1#{age := 31},

%% Pattern matching extraction
#{name := Name} = Map2.
maps.notes: Maps use `#{}` syntax. `=>` adds or updates, while `:=` updates only if the key strictly exists or matches in patterns.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
%% Try/Catch
safe_div(X, Y) ->
    try X / Y of
        Result -> Result
    catch
        error:badarith -> 0
    end.

%% Let it crash philosophy
%% Caller processes link to workers and restart them on failure.
error_handling.notes: While try/catch exists, idiomatic Erlang uses "Let It Crash"—isolating failures in supervised processes rather than defensive programming.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
% Line comment in Erlang
-doc("Function doc").
add(A, B) -> A + B.
comments.notes: Erlang uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Erlang supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.code:
IsActive = true,
Result = IsActive andalso not false.
booleans.notes: Erlang treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Erlang performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Erlang represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Erlang formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.code:
case Response of
    {ok, Data} -> Data;
    {error, _} -> error
end.
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Erlang, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Erlang constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: Erlang achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: Erlang emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Erlang are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Erlang uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Erlang provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: Erlang isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
